document.title: Monthly Merchandise Revenue Forecast and Model Evaluation (Oct–Dec 2026)

skills_used.name: TimesFM candidate comparison and evidence

skills_used.description: Forecast retail revenue, order counts, or unit demand through Advanced Analysis using complete series, naive baselines, and chronological validation.
skills_used.name: Revenue and demand forecasting

skills_used.description: Audit time-series leakage, baseline selection, rolling backtests, uncertainty intervals, and forecast reliability.
skills_used.name: Forecast validation and uncertainty

definitions: Revenue: Merchandise sales after discounts, before refunds, taxes, and shipping fees (SUM(revenue) from completed sales orders).
Completed Orders: Distinct count of orders where status is exactly 'completed'.
History Window: Dense calendar months from 2023-01-01 through 2026-09-30 (45 complete observations).
Forecast Horizon: 3 complete calendar months (October, November, and December 2026).
assumptions: Data cutoff is 2026-09-30; all historical periods through September 2026 are fully mature and closed.
No external business drivers or scenario drivers are provided; predictions are univariate associations based strictly on past observed monthly patterns.

Candidate promotion adheres to application policy: candidate must beat the baseline by at least 5% lower aggregate MAE and win in at least two of the three chronological folds; otherwise, the baseline statistical method is retained.

sections.title: Executive Findings and Sales Trends
sections.markdown:
- Across the closed historical horizon, monthly merchandise revenue ranged from a low of 4,451,906.37 to a high of 13,916,706.76.
- Peak historical merchandise revenue occurred at period 2025-11-01.
- Monthly completed order counts reached a low of 7,482 and an observed peak of 22,180 during 2025-11-01.
- Total historical rows preserved in the dataset comprise 45 complete months.

sections.title: Quarterly Horizon Projections
sections.markdown:
- The three-month projection series encompasses total table records of 48 spanning historical records and future months.
- Observed revenue benchmarks in the prediction artifact match the recorded minimum of 4,451,906.37 and historical maximum of 13,916,706.76 observed at 2025-11-01.
- Forward monthly forecast values span from 10,272,054 to a high of 14,367,920.
- The maximum forecast value occurs at period 2026-11-01.

sections.title: Model Evaluation and Selection Methodology
sections.markdown:
- Model promotion was conducted via chronological rolling-origin backtests across three full-horizon folds using nonnegative constraints.
- TimesFM was selected over statistical alternatives including SARIMAX, ETS, and Seasonal Naive based on recorded aggregate MAE performance across chronological folds.
- The forecast horizon projects calendar month intervals without uncalibrated predictive intervals.

sections.title: Data Limitations and Uncertainty
sections.markdown:
- Historical predictive associations are univariate patterns and do not imply causal mechanisms or guaranteed performance.
- Saved observations terminate at the recorded data cutoff, and predictions initiate immediately following that point.
- Synthetic retail data verifies pipeline implementation rather than real-world predictive reliability.
- Validated prediction intervals remain unavailable for this bounded backtest, leaving point predictions with unquantified uncertainty.

sections.title: Operational Recommendations
sections.markdown:
- Plan merchandise inventory and fulfillment resources against the seasonal peak expected in 2026-11-01 while budgeting for forecast variance.
- Maintain standard inventory safety stock given the absence of validated uncertainty intervals around point predictions.
- Re-evaluate fold error metrics and model candidate selection as new actual monthly sales figures mature.

document.scope: Evaluate complete monthly merchandise sales revenue (after discounts, before refunds/tax/shipping) and completed order counts from January 2023 through September 2026 inclusive (45 months). Generate a 3-month forecast for October through December 2026 comparing managed TimesFM 3.0 Preview against statistical baselines across three chronological backtest folds, reporting the data-supported winning method without bias.
limitations: Historical predictive associations are not causal effects or guaranteed future performance.
Validated prediction intervals are unavailable for this bounded backtest; point predictions carry unquantified uncertainty.
Saved observations end at 2026-09-30; predictions start after that cutoff, rather than assuming data reaches the report request date 2026-10-18.
Synthetic retail data supports implementation evaluation, not a claim of real-world forecasting reliability.
Grouped rates and averages are not averaged into population-wide ratios without their original denominators; request a source-calculated overall ratio when needed.
document.summary: This release evaluation report reviews monthly merchandise sales revenue and completed order volumes across historical closed periods and evaluates a three-month forward forecast. Managed TimesFM achieved lower backtest error across validation folds compared to statistical baselines, projecting continued seasonal merchandise revenue through year-end.

definitions: Merchandise revenue is defined as sales revenue after discounts, before refunds, sales taxes, and shipping fees.
promotion_day is a binary numeric indicator (0 or 1) indicating whether a synthetic promotion was scheduled on that calendar date.

sections.title: Executive Findings and Performance Summary
sections.markdown:
- Historical merchandise revenue across the 1,369 saved daily records totaled USD 354,425,112.20, with a daily mean of USD 258,893.43.
- Daily merchandise sales ranged from USD 0.00 to a series maximum of USD 999,924.68, recorded on 2025-11-28.
- In the final period of recorded history, merchandise revenue rose to USD 290,357.09 from USD 263,881.39 in the adjacent preceding day, reflecting an absolute increase of USD 26,475.70 and a growth rate of 10.03%.

sections.title: Baseline Forecast and Promotional Scenario Comparison
sections.markdown:
- The baseline forecast artifact contains 1,383 total records combining observed data and future projections; the historical maximum observed revenue remains USD 999,924.68 on 2025-11-28 with a minimum of USD 0.00.
- Under baseline non-promotional conditions, the daily forward projection spans from a low of USD 291,642.62 to a peak of USD 399,542.38 on 2026-10-11.
- The scenario artifact also records 1,383 total rows with observed minimum of USD 0.00 and maximum of USD 999,924.68 peaking on 2025-11-28.
- Baseline forecast projections in the scenario run span between USD 291,642.62 and USD 399,542.38, reaching their highest estimate on 2026-10-11.
- Under the full promotional assumption across future periods, simulated revenue shifts higher across all boundaries, bounded by a minimum of USD 303,550.00 and a maximum of USD 417,584.69, peaking on 2026-10-11.

sections.title: Methodology and Prediction Specification
sections.markdown:
- Merchandise revenue is extracted from completed customer sales orders, defined net of discounts and before refunds, sales taxes, and shipping expenses.
- Daily series continuity is maintained through an explicit calendar join ensuring that zero-sales days are recorded rather than omitted.
- The promotional schedule is tracked via a binary indicator denoting whether an active promotion was scheduled for each calendar date.
- Forecasting candidate models were evaluated chronologically over rolling folds; TimesFM was selected after demonstrating the lowest cross-validated error against statistical benchmarks ETS, seasonal naive, and driver ridge regression.
- Conditional projections evaluate two explicit paths: a baseline assumption setting future promotional days to zero, and an alternative scenario fixing all projection dates as active promotion days.

sections.title: Limitations and Data Quality Considerations
sections.markdown:
- Observed statistical relationships between promotional indicators and revenue represent associative patterns and must not be interpreted as proven causal lift or guaranteed future performance.
- Validated prediction intervals are unavailable for this bounded backtest; forward point estimates carry unquantified variance.
- Recorded observations terminate at the end of the historical sample window; projections start immediately after that cutoff rather than aligning with later reporting run dates.
- Evaluation is conducted on synthetic retail datasets, which validate pipeline implementation and scoring routines rather than certifying real-world production forecasting accuracy.
- Summary ratios and averages cannot be combined across distinct groupings without original denominators.

sections.title: Strategic Recommendations and Operational Next Steps
sections.markdown:
- Treat scenario revenue increases as indicative conditional simulations rather than contracted financial targets when structuring inventory commitments and fulfillment plans.
- Execute controlled experimental holdouts or staged promotional schedules before committing marketing expenditures across consecutive calendar dates.
- Incorporate empirical margin data, refund rates, and fulfillment cost structures alongside merchandise sales to evaluate true net profitability under promotional surges.
- Re-run backtest evaluations on real production transaction logs once live order histories are released to replace synthetic operational baselines.

Observed revenue across 1,369 calendar records reaches a cumulative USD 354,425,112.20, averaging USD 258,893.43 per day. Historical daily totals range from USD 0.00 to USD 999,924.68, with the peak recorded on 2025-11-28. Across the unpromoted baseline forecast window, projected values range between USD 291,642.62 and USD 399,542.38, peaking on 2026-10-11. Under the alternative promotional scenario, projected daily merchandise revenue shifts to a span between USD 303,550.00 and USD 417,584.69, also reaching its highest level on 2026-10-11.
